title: Finite coefficients on the pro-etale site
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme and $\Lambda$ a finite ring with the discrete topology. Work in the universes and the small skeleton of the small pro-etale site $T_{\Proet}$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Modules mean left modules. For an object $U\to T$, let $\pi_0(|U|)$ be the set of connected components of the underlying topological space $|U|$, with the quotient topology: a subset is open precisely when its inverse image in $|U|$ is open. Write $\operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0(|U|),\Lambda)$ for the ring of continuous functions, with pointwise operations. A morphism $V\to U$ induces a map $\pi_0(|V|)\to\pi_0(|U|)$, and restriction of functions is precomposition with that map. Define the coefficient sheaf of rings by sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of this presheaf:

$$
 \Lambda_{T,\Proet}=\bigl(U\longmapsto\operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0(|U|),\Lambda)\bigr)^\#.
$$

Let $\Mod(T_{\Proet},\Lambda)=\Mod(\Lambda_{T,\Proet})$ be the abelian category of sheaves of modules over this ring sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Its morphisms are morphisms of abelian sheaves that are $\Lambda_{T,\Proet}(U)$-linear on each object $U$. Define its derived category using [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]:

$$
 D(T_{\Proet},\Lambda)=\mathsf{Cpx}(\Mod(T_{\Proet},\Lambda))
 [\{\text{quasi-isomorphisms}\}^{-1}],
$$

where $\mathsf{Cpx}$ means cochain complexes indexed by $\mathbf Z$, and a quasi-isomorphism induces an isomorphism on every cohomology sheaf $\mathcal H^i=\ker d^i/\operatorname{im}d^{i-1}$ in this abelian category. The full subcategory $\Dplus(T_{\Proet},\Lambda)$ consists of the objects $K$ for which some $a\in\mathbf Z$ satisfies $\mathcal H^i(K)=0$ for all $i<a$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories].

Let $T_{\Et}$ be the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and let $\Lambda_{T,\Et}$ be the sheafification of the constant presheaf of rings $\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Set $D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)=D(\Mod(\Lambda_{T,\Et}))$ by the same abstract derived-category construction; for commutative $\Lambda$ this is exactly [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. The comparison geometric morphism $\nu_T:T_{\Proet}\to T_{\Et}$ and its inverse image on $\Lambda$-module sheaves are those of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Write $\nu_T^*:D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)\to D(T_{\Proet},\Lambda)$ for the functor induced by applying that exact module inverse image termwise to complexes [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated].

Define $\Dbc(T_{\Proet},\Lambda)$ to be the strictly full subcategory consisting of objects $K$ admitting an etale complex $L$ and an isomorphism

$$
 \nu_T^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}K,
$$

where $L$ is bounded constructible: there are integers $a\le b$ with $\mathcal H^i(L)=0$ outside $[a,b]$, and for each $i$ there is a finite stratification of $T$ by locally closed subschemes [def-constructible-stratification] whose images are constructible subsets [def-weil-constructible-subset], on each of which the restriction of $\mathcal H^i(L)$ is etale locally isomorphic to a constant sheaf associated to a finite left $\Lambda$-module. For commutative $\Lambda$, this is precisely the bounded constructible etale criterion of [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]; the same explicitly stated criterion defines the notation for a noncommutative finite ring. Morphisms in both full subcategories are all the morphisms between their objects in $D(T_{\Proet},\Lambda)$.
